Kings places the pronoun after Manasseh's sins and says the Lord was unwilling to be propitiated. This proposed direct parallel remains unretained because the perpetrator attribution and judgment wording are not harmonized.

source_verse.text: and because of the innocent blood that Jehoiakim shed, filling Jerusalem with innocent blood; yet the Lord did not wish to destroy them.

target_verses.text: He also shed innocent blood and filled Jerusalem with innocent blood, and the Lord was unwilling to be propitiated.

known_pending_target_candidates.reason: The age, approximate reign length, and evil assessment closely correspond, but Chronicles names Jechonias and adds ten days, while the supplied Kings record calls both father and successor Joakim. The personal-name issue is not resolved by this pass and this target is unretained.

source_verse.text: Jechonias was eighteen years old when he began to reign, and he reigned three months and ten days in Jerusalem. He did what was evil before the Lord.

target_verses.text: Joakim was eighteen years old when he became king, and he reigned three months in Jerusalem. His mother’s name was Nestha daughter of Ellanathan, from Jerusalem.
He did what was evil in the Lord’s eyes, according to everything his father had done.

known_pending_target_candidates.reason: Both narratives concern installation of Zedekiah/Sedekias by Babylon's king, but Chronicles calls him the preceding king's father's brother and Kings calls Maththanias his son. This direct identity-and-kinship proposal is unretained rather than harmonizing the supplied relationship.

source_verse.text: At the turn of the year King Nebuchadnezzar sent and brought him into Babylon with the desirable vessels of the Lord’s house. He made Zedekiah, his father’s brother, king over Judah and Jerusalem.

target_verses.text: The king of Babylon made Maththanias, his son, king in his place and gave him the name Sedekias.
